no quantifier over field extensions and no `GeometricallyReduced` class. Compare
`smooth_of_forall_isReduced` directly above, which asks for one reducedness statement *per*
field extension of `k`: this asks for one, at the algebraic closure.

WHY THIS IS A STRICT IMPROVEMENT AND NOT A RESTATEMENT. `GeometricallyReduced` is *defined*
by base change along every `Spec K ⟶ Spec k`, so it implies the `k̄` instance; the converse
— reducedness over `k̄` implies reducedness over every field extension — is the transcendental
half of the descent, and it is **absent from mathlib v4.31**: there is no producer, and
`GeometricallyReduced` has no `MorphismProperty.DescendsAlong` instance (checked from this
side and independently by the sibling project; inbox I-0495, 2026-07-28). So the two
hypotheses are *not* interchangeable, and this one is the weaker.

internally, but through a `private` lemma, so the intermediate statement is unreachable by
name. Both projects had recorded "get `smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed` made public" as the

/-- The **pullback action** on a family of divisors along `ψ : T' ⟶ T` of
`Over S`: pull the sheaf and the quotient map back along
`quotBaseMap π ψ : X_{T'} ⟶ X_T`, matching the `O`-side through
`pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)` — exactly
`QuotFamily.pullbackAlong` at `E = O_X`.  The divisor condition base-changes
by `Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial`
(`lem:relative_divisor_base_change`). -/
noncomputable def pullbackAlong {T T' : Over S} (ψ : T' ⟶ T)
    (x : DivFamily π T) : DivFamily π T' where
  F := (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).obj x.F
  isFinitePresentation :=
    Modules.pullback_isFinitePresentation _ x.F x.isFinitePresentation
  flat := fun {_} hU {_} hV e =>
    CoherentSheafFlat.of_isPullback (quotBaseSquare π ψ) x.F
      (letI := x.isFinitePresentation; inferInstance) x.flat hU hV e
  properSupport :=
    Modules.HasProperSupport.of_isPullback (quotBaseSquare π ψ) x.F
      x.isFinitePresentation x.properSupport
  q := (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
      (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv ≫
    (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map x.q
  epi :=
    @CategoryTheory.epi_comp _ _ _ _ _
      (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv inferInstance
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map x.q)
      (@CategoryTheory.Functor.map_epi _ _ _ _
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)) inferInstance _ _ x.q x.epi)
  kerLocallyTrivial :=
    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial.of_iso
      (kernelIsIsoComp
        (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
          (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map x.q)).symm

          (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) inferInstance)

1	/-

     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Geometrically.Integral
     7	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Smooth
     8	import Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.FractionRing
     9	import Mathlib.RingTheory.RingHom.StandardSmooth
    10	import Mathlib.RingTheory.Smooth.Flat
    11	import Mathlib.RingTheory.Unramified.Field
    12	
    13	/-!
    14	# Smooth morphisms are geometrically reduced
    15	
    16	A smooth morphism of schemes is geometrically reduced: every base change to the spectrum of a
    17	field is reduced. Combined with geometric irreducibility, this upgrades the standing hypotheses
    18	of the Jacobian challenge (`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom` and
    19	`GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom`) to `GeometricallyIntegral C.hom`, which is what all the
    20	actual geometry of the project consumes.
    21	
    22	The commutative-algebra core is that a standard smooth algebra over a domain is reduced. By the
    23	structure theorem for standard smooth algebras (Stacks 00T7,
    24	`RingHom.IsStandardSmooth.exists_etale_mvPolynomial`), such an algebra `S` is étale over a
    25	polynomial ring `P` over the base. Since `S` is flat over the domain `P`, it embeds into
    26	`Frac(P) ⊗[P] S`, which is formally unramified and essentially of finite type over the field
    27	`Frac(P)`, hence reduced by `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_field`.
    28	
    29	## Main results
    30	
    31	* `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_isDomain`: a flat, formally unramified algebra,
    32	  essentially of finite type over a domain, is reduced.
    33	* `Algebra.Etale.isReduced_of_isDomain`, `RingHom.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain`,
    34	  `Algebra.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain`: étale/standard smooth algebras over
    35	  domains are reduced.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.isReduced_of_field`: a scheme smooth over `Spec` of a field is
    37	  reduced.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.geometricallyReduced`: a smooth morphism is geometrically reduced
    39	  (instance), together with the `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` variant.
    40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.geometricallyIntegral`: a smooth, geometrically irreducible
    41	  morphism is geometrically integral (instance), together with the
    42	  `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` variant.
    43	
    44	This file is written in mathlib generality and is a candidate for upstreaming. It was
    45	developed in the sibling project `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`
    46	(`AlgebraicJacobian/Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean`) and imported here unchanged; it
    47	depends on Mathlib only, so the two copies can be kept in step by file copy until one
    48	of them is upstreamed.
    49	
    50	In this project it closes the geometric-integrality half of the headline's hypothesis
    51	gap: `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` and `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian` are stated for a
    52	smooth proper **geometrically irreducible** curve, while the Picard/FGA development
    53	runs under `GeometricallyIntegral`. `Smooth.geometricallyIntegral` bridges the two, so
    54	the only remaining hypothesis gap at the headline is the `k`-rational point, which is a
    55	genuine mathematical gap rather than missing infrastructure (see
    56	`AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean`, leaf `hasRationalPoint_of_curve`).
    57	-/
    58	
    59	set_option autoImplicit false
    60	
    61	universe u
    62	
    63	open TensorProduct
    64	
    65	section RingTheory
    66	
    67	/-- A flat, formally unramified algebra, essentially of finite type over a domain, is reduced.
    68	This generalizes `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_field` from fields to domains, at the
    69	price of the flatness assumption (which is automatic over a field). -/
    70	theorem Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_isDomain (B S : Type*) [CommRing B] [CommRing S]
    71	    [IsDomain B] [Algebra B S] [Algebra.FormallyUnramified B S] [Algebra.EssFiniteType B S]
    72	    [Module.Flat B S] : IsReduced S := by
    73	  have : IsReduced (FractionRing B ⊗[B] S) :=
    74	    Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_field (FractionRing B) (FractionRing B ⊗[B] S)
    75	  refine isReduced_of_injective
    76	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := B) (A := FractionRing B) (B := S)) ?_
    77	  have h : ⇑(Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := B) (A := FractionRing B) (B := S)) =
    78	      ⇑(LinearMap.rTensor S (Algebra.ofId B (FractionRing B)).toLinearMap) ∘
    79	        ⇑(TensorProduct.lid B S).symm := by
    80	    ext s
    81	    simp
    82	  rw [h]
    83	  exact (Module.Flat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _
    84	    (IsFractionRing.injective B (FractionRing B))).comp (TensorProduct.lid B S).symm.injective
    85	
    86	/-- An étale algebra over a domain is reduced. -/
    87	theorem Algebra.Etale.isReduced_of_isDomain (B S : Type*) [CommRing B] [CommRing S] [IsDomain B]
    88	    [Algebra B S] [Algebra.Etale B S] : IsReduced S :=
    89	  Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_isDomain B S
    90	
    91	/-- The target of a standard smooth ring homomorphism out of a domain is reduced: by
    92	Stacks 00T7 it is étale over a polynomial ring over the base, and étale algebras over
    93	domains are reduced. -/
    94	theorem RingHom.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain {B S : Type*} [CommRing B] [CommRing S]
    95	    [IsDomain B] {g : B →+* S} (hg : g.IsStandardSmooth) : IsReduced S := by
    96	  obtain ⟨n, φ, -, hφ⟩ := hg.exists_etale_mvPolynomial
    97	  algebraize [φ]
    98	  exact Algebra.Etale.isReduced_of_isDomain (MvPolynomial (Fin n) B) S
    99	
   100	/-- A standard smooth algebra over a domain is reduced. -/
   101	theorem Algebra.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain (B S : Type*) [CommRing B] [CommRing S]
   102	    [IsDomain B] [Algebra B S] [Algebra.IsStandardSmooth B S] : IsReduced S :=
   103	  (RingHom.isStandardSmooth_algebraMap.mpr ‹_›).isReduced_of_isDomain
   104	
   105	end RingTheory
   106	
   107	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   108	
   109	open CategoryTheory Limits
   110	
   111	variable {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
   112	
   113	/-- A scheme smooth over the spectrum of a field is reduced. -/
   114	theorem Smooth.isReduced_of_field {K : Type u} [Field K] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [Smooth f] :
   115	    IsReduced X := by
   116	  have hsub : Subsingleton (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
   117	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum K))
   118	  choose U hU V hV hxV e hsm using Smooth.exists_isStandardSmooth f
   119	  -- Each chart is the spectrum of a standard smooth algebra over (a ring isomorphic to) `K`,
   120	  -- hence reduced.
   121	  have hred (x : X) : IsReduced (V x).toScheme := by
   122	    have : IsAffine (V x).toScheme := hV x
   123	    have hfx : f x ∈ U x := e x (hxV x)
   124	    have hUx : U x = ⊤ := by
   125	      refine TopologicalSpace.Opens.ext (Set.eq_univ_of_forall fun y ↦ ?_)
   126	      exact Subsingleton.elim (f x) y ▸ hfx
   127	    have hdom : IsDomain Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), U x) := by
   128	      rw [hUx]
   129	      exact Function.Injective.isDomain
   130	        (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv (RingEquiv.injective _)
   131	    have hΓ : _root_.IsReduced Γ(X, V x) := (hsm x).isReduced_of_isDomain
   132	    have : _root_.IsReduced Γ((V x).toScheme, ⊤) :=
   133	      isReduced_of_injective (V x).topIso.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv (RingEquiv.injective _)
   134	    exact isReduced_of_isAffine_isReduced _
   135	  let 𝒰 : X.OpenCover := Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers X (fun x ↦ (V x).toScheme) (fun x ↦ (V x).ι)
   136	    (fun x ↦ ⟨x, ⟨x, hxV x⟩, rfl⟩) (fun x ↦ inferInstance)
   137	  have : ∀ i, IsReduced (𝒰.X i) := hred
   138	  exact IsReduced.of_openCover _ 𝒰
   139	
   140	/-- A smooth morphism of schemes is geometrically reduced: every base change to the spectrum
   141	of a field is smooth over that field, hence reduced. -/
   142	instance (priority := 100) Smooth.geometricallyReduced (f : X ⟶ Y) [Smooth f] :
   143	    GeometricallyReduced f where
   144	  geometrically_isReduced := fun K _ y Z fst snd h ↦
   145	    have : Smooth snd := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @Smooth) h ‹Smooth f›
   146	    Smooth.isReduced_of_field snd
   147	
   148	/-- A morphism smooth of relative dimension `1` is smooth. This is the relative dimension of
   149	the curve bundle of the Jacobian challenge; the general statement is
   150	`SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth`, which cannot be an instance since `n` does not occur in
   151	the conclusion. -/
   152	instance (priority := 100) Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one (f : X ⟶ Y)
   153	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] : Smooth f :=
   154	  SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth 1 f
   155	
   156	/-- A morphism smooth of some relative dimension is geometrically reduced. Not an instance
   157	since `n` cannot be inferred from the conclusion; for relative dimension `1`, instance
   158	resolution goes through `Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`. -/
   159	theorem SmoothOfRelativeDimension.geometricallyReduced (n : ℕ) (f : X ⟶ Y)
   160	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension n f] : GeometricallyReduced f :=
   161	  have : Smooth f := SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth n f
   162	  inferInstance
   163	
   164	/-- A smooth, geometrically irreducible morphism is geometrically integral. -/
   165	instance (priority := 100) Smooth.geometricallyIntegral (f : X ⟶ Y) [Smooth f]
   166	    [GeometricallyIrreducible f] : GeometricallyIntegral f :=
   167	  .of_geometricallyReduced_of_geometricallyIrreducible f
   168	
   169	/-- A geometrically irreducible morphism, smooth of some relative dimension, is geometrically
   170	integral. Not an instance since `n` cannot be inferred from the conclusion. -/
   171	theorem SmoothOfRelativeDimension.geometricallyIntegral (n : ℕ) (f : X ⟶ Y)
   172	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension n f] [GeometricallyIrreducible f] : GeometricallyIntegral f :=
   173	  have : Smooth f := SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth n f
   174	  .of_geometricallyReduced_of_geometricallyIrreducible f

no quantifier over field extensions and no `GeometricallyReduced` class. Compare
`smooth_of_forall_isReduced` directly above, which asks for one reducedness statement *per*
field extension of `k`: this asks for one, at the algebraic closure.

WHY THIS IS A STRICT IMPROVEMENT AND NOT A RESTATEMENT. `GeometricallyReduced` is *defined*
by base change along every `Spec K ⟶ Spec k`, so it implies the `k̄` instance; the converse
— reducedness over `k̄` implies reducedness over every field extension — is the transcendental
half of the descent, and it is **absent from mathlib v4.31**: there is no producer, and
`GeometricallyReduced` has no `MorphismProperty.DescendsAlong` instance (checked from this
side and independently by the sibling project; inbox I-0495, 2026-07-28). So the two
hypotheses are *not* interchangeable, and this one is the weaker.

HOW IT IS AVAILABLE AT ALL. Mathlib's own `smooth_of_grpObj` reduces to exactly the `k̄` case
internally, but through a `private` lemma, so the intermediate statement is unreachable by
name. Both projects had recorded "get `smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed` made public" as the
cheap upstream route. That PR is unnecessary: `private` hides the name and not the proof, and
--- 1405,1420 ---

/-- **Properness of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` from universal closedness of the ambient `Pic_{C/k}`** —
proved (run 0067). The composite of `universallyClosed_of_ambient` with
`proper_of_universallyClosed`.

This is the sharpest form of the properness reduction currently available: `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is
proper over `k` as soon as `Pic_{C/k}` is universally closed over `k`. Both the separatedness
and finite-type conjuncts of `IsProper`, and the passage from the ambient scheme to the
identity component, are discharged; what remains is one property of `Pic_{C/k}`, which is
where Kleiman §5 Thm.~`th:qpp&p` speaks. -/
